title: The Cost of a Small Lie
paragraphs: To avoid an uncomfortable conversation, Samira once told her manager a minor lie about why a project was delayed, a decision that felt harmless and easily forgettable at the time she made it.
The lie, however, required a second small lie a week later to remain consistent, and Samira found herself uneasily tracking which version of events she had told to which colleague.
What had begun as a single convenient shortcut gradually evolved into a small but persistent source of anxiety, as she worried constantly about contradicting herself in front of the wrong person.

Eventually, the inconsistency surfaced during an unrelated meeting, and Samira had to admit the original lie, an uncomfortable conversation made considerably worse by the additional layer of dishonesty built on top of it.
Her manager was more disappointed by the dishonesty than by the original delay itself, which had been entirely explainable and forgivable had she simply been honest about it from the very beginning.
Samira later reflected that the small, seemingly harmless lie had cost her far more trust and peace of mind than any honest, uncomfortable conversation ever could have cost her.
